\section{Foundations}

\begin{frame}{Plain theorem}
  \begin{theorem}[Pythagoras]
    If \(a\) and \(b\) are the legs of a right triangle, then
    \(a^2+b^2=c^2\).
  \end{theorem}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Definition and example}
  \begin{definition}
    A square is a rectangle with four equal sides.
  \end{definition}

  \begin{example}
    The unit square has area one.
  \end{example}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Custom declaration}
  \begin{proposition}
    Every square is a rectangle.
  \end{proposition}
\end{frame}

\begin{frame}{Proof template}
  \begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
    This follows immediately from the definition.
  \end{proof}
\end{frame}

    Covered theorem material keeps its place.
  \end{lemma}
\end{frame}
